title: Private instance adoption signal profiles & quarterly sprint plan
creator: Priya Khanna
description:
Goal: Define a minimal, actionable set of adoption signals and a quarterly sprint mapping so Sales/Onboarding and Engineering can measure private (VPC / on‑prem) tenant readiness and automate activation gating.

Why now: customers onboarding isolated instances have variable integration paths (networking, KMS, telemetry). We need standardized signals so we can: 1) surface health to internal stakeholders 2) automate gating for staged activations and runbooks and 3) feed OKR-level dashboards for adoption rate / time-to-first-successful-inference.

Scope: signal definitions (what to collect and how to compute), privacy/anonymization constraints, dashboard and alert design, integration points with the Console (tenant readiness API), and a sprint-level roadmap for Q2 to deliver detection, visualization, and runbook automation. Excludes deep instrumentation work that requires kernel-level runtime changes (tracked in ENG-2789).
acceptance_criteria: Signal catalog published in Confluence with clear definitions, collection method, compute formula, and sensitivity classification
Grafana readiness dashboard prototype showing per-tenant heatmap + 4 core signals
Console readiness API spec merged (OpenAPI) and stub endpoint implemented for Private control plane
Two onboarding runbooks updated to use signals for gating + corresponding PagerDuty escalation mappings
Telemetry collection conforms to KMS/PII guidance; security review completed and signoff obtained
milestones: M1 - 2026-03-24: Draft signal catalog and privacy classification (team review)
M2 - 2026-04-07: Engineering implements lightweight metrics emitter (stub) + Console readiness API spec
M3 - 2026-05-05: Dashboard prototype (heatmap + drilldowns) + first cohort internal trial
M4 - 2026-05-28: Runbooks updated, automation rules for gating merged, security signoff
M5 - 2026-06-14: Finalize metrics sampling, public runbook template, and OKR dashboard feed
risks: Inconsistent agent SDK versions across customer environments may delay reliable signal collection
Telemetry containing tenant identifiers raises compliance questions until KMS guidance is finalized
Engineering bandwidth conflicts (kernel/runtime work) could push M2 by 2+ weeks
Over-alerting on immature signals may desensitize Onboarding and SRE teams
notes: Design principle: signals should be composable (scoreable) and graded so we can tune thresholds by customer cohort
We will prioritize signals that do not require kernel patches: network handshake completion, KMS key availability, control plane webhook ack, first inference latency sample
Proposed scoring: 0-100 readiness index combining binary checks (network, KMS) and rolling metrics (latency, error-rate)
Privacy approach: store only hashed tenant IDs for aggregated dashboards; raw tenant identifiers will be confined to secure logs with KMS encryption
